comments.html:
Thanks for the highlight! Happy that you find it interesting!

Note that the core of the STP implementation is the MSTPD project, not me. It has a clean design allowing it to be compiled to WebAssembly by adding some glue.

I think this is the article I spend the most time as of today, but it was quite fun. And informative. Many documents around STP does not really highlight the fact that the protocol is pretty distributed. They start from the root and show how the BPDUs propagate. But in reality, the other half of the network has already made their opinion on the topology. It took me some time to find a way to allow a reader to even follow the explanations with all the BPDUs moving at the same time.
comments.name: Vincent Bernat

comments.html: Ivan, you're right that this is the kind of interactive explanation STP has always deserved. Walking through the WebAssembly implementation and seeing the topology converge step by step makes the root election click in a way static diagrams never did for me. It reminded me of exam prep, where time management matters as much as knowledge, which is why I liked the Study4Pass exam-day playbook on beating the clock in timed IT certification tests. The video version is a nice touch too for those who prefer watching over reading.
